text: A minute ago, this assistant read both of my memories.
Now it reads none. I did not ask it to forget. I revoked one key.
That is satchel. Your assistant's memory, sealed to your passkey.
Every assistant today makes you pick. Start each chat knowing nothing about you, or keep a file on you that the vendor holds.
ChatGPT's own help page lists what its memory draws on: past chats, saved memories, files, even Gmail. And ChatGPT decides which of it is relevant.
And that memory is stuck there. The next app you try starts from zero.
Any team adding memory to an assistant meets this same choice. Satchel is the third option, and it ships as a package.
Satchel turns it around. Pip is the assistant. It seals each fact on your device, under a key only your passkey can make. Storage holds ciphertext.
Fern, a second app, reads only through a grant. The grant is a wrapped key, recorded in a registry contract on Monad.
Revoke moves the folder to the next epoch. Pip seals every memory again. The key Fern holds opens nothing, and its next read fails with grant revoked.
cap: Revoke moves the folder to the next epoch. Pip seals every memory again. The key Fern holds opens nothing, and its next read fails with GRANT_REVOKED.

text: Why Monad? Grants and epochs have to sit where every app can read them and no app can rewrite them. A grant costs about one hundredth of a MON, and the revoke less.
cap: Why Monad? Grants and epochs have to sit where every app can read them and no app can rewrite them. A grant costs about 0.012 MON, and the revoke less.

text: The registry has nineteen tests and two invariants. A mutation run breaks it six ways, and goes red six times.
cap: The registry has 19 tests and 2 invariants. A mutation run breaks it six ways, and goes red six times.

text: The S D K has eighty-nine tests. A fresh project installs it from the tarball and runs the whole flow against the live registry.
cap: The SDK has 89 tests. A fresh project installs it from the tarball and runs the whole flow against the live registry.

text: Developers get all of it in one install: npm install satchel S D K. Seal, grant, revoke.
cap: Developers get all of it in one install: npm install satchel-sdk. Seal, grant, revoke.

text: We built every layer ourselves: the contract, the S D K, and the two apps that use them. Your memory should follow you between apps, and end when you say so.
